title: Spring warmth gave no clear repeated link to butterfly flight-tail balance in England and Wales in 1985-2024
abstract: We tested whether March-May warmth changed the balance between late and early recorded butterfly flight dates. Eight site-effect models used 32,999 site-species-years for Meadow Brown and Ringlet in England and Wales in 1985-2024. Models controlled winter temperature, spring rain, linear time and peak count. All eight adjusted delete-year jackknife intervals included zero. Five checks also gave intervals across zero in every sample. The data do not establish a repeated temperature link to this measure of season shape. They do not establish equal responses of early and late tails. Selected sites, shared count errors, missing visits, coarse weather and only 20 annual exposures per model limit inference. This is an exploratory follow-up on records used in prior campaign work. The package gives code, model summaries, exact source hashes, numerical checks and a figure. External databases remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Spring temperature slopes for late minus early recorded flight tails. All eight adjusted intervals include zero.
